newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy soft wheat output in 1997 seen down 13.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Italy soft wheat output in 1997 seen down 13.5 pct.

text.p: Italy's autumn-sown soft wheat harvest in 1997 is seen falling 13.5 percent to some 3.38 million tonnes, the Italian Institute for Agricultural Studies (ISMEA) said in its latest forecasts.
ISMEA attributed the fall in production to a 7.4 percent drop in area and a 6.6 percent fall in yields.

"Even though the fall in areas sown could be misunderstood given the reduction in the set-aside allowed by the European Union (down to five percent from 10 percent)...the major reason for the lower sowings were climatic conditions with sporadic rain which prevented plantings in the usual period," ISMEA said.
"Furthermore, in the sowing period soft wheat market prices were rather depressed and this caused a shift from soft wheat to oilseeds and spring sowings," ISMEA added.
Durum wheat production in 1997 is seen falling 4.2 percent to 4.23 million tonnes, despite a 2.2 percent increase in sowings. ISMEA said this was due to a 6.2 percent fall in average yields.
Barley production is forecast to fall 14 percent to 1.17 million tonnes with a 7.9 percent drop in area and a 6.6 percent fall in average yields.

ISMEA noted that its forecasts were conducted up to May 20, around a month and a half before the main harvest period. It added that there should not be any major changes to the estimates after this date due to weather conditions since the May 20 date.
